# plan:nav-ssr-dashboard — deliverable (item 1; /login loop and localhost-guard follow as separate commits)

Coder: pij-local-parakeet (coder/ssr-dashboard) · Request 01a1cd15-c447-7b51-a19e-0b30752a1427

## Commit on main

- `e37b1ea0d` fix(web): server-render the dashboard shell and pages

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/features/063-login/components/auth-provider.tsx` | `SessionProvider` rendered directly, no `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` |
| `apps/web/next.config.mjs` | `next-auth` removed from `serverExternalPackages`; `turbopack.resolveAlias` `next/navigation.js` → `next/navigation` |
| `apps/web/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` | `<Suspense>` around the page, so the shell streams before page data |
| `test/unit/web/features/063-login/dashboard-shell-ssr.test.tsx` | new: server render of the real dashboard layout must contain the sidebar and the page |
| `docs/domains/_platform/auth/domain.md` | contract and history row |

## Cause, confirmed

- Original build (main at 0aebeb1): `/workspaces/chainglass` HTML with JS disabled has 0 characters of text, no sidebar, no `<main>`.
- Variant A, plain `SessionProvider` with `next-auth` still external: HTTP 500, server log `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState')` ×3. That is the React-resolution problem the old comment described.
- Bundling `next-auth` fixes SSR, but the build then fails: `Failed to collect configuration for /api/file-notes ... app-route/vendored/contexts/app-router-context.js, file not found`. Cause: `patches/next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32.patch` rewrites `next/navigation` to `next/navigation.js` for Node ESM (vitest needs that). In a bundle the `.js` path skips Next's per-layer alias. The Turbopack alias points it back, and the patch stays.

## Acceptance evidence

Prod build, headless Chromium, `/workspaces/chainglass`, 5 measured runs after a warm-up. The load average is quoted with each run.

| | Before (Jordan's 10:00 build of 0aebeb1, served on :3101) | After (fft build of this change, served on :3101) |
|---|---|---|
| First contentful paint, median | 4344 ms | 48 ms |
| FCP range | 1524–5572 ms | 24–64 ms |
| Load average during runs | 74–100 | 259–280 |
| TTFB, median | 7 ms | 8 ms |
| Document complete, median | 4300 ms | 6817 ms (page data; niced server at load 260+) |
| HTML text with JS disabled | 0 chars, no sidebar, no main | sidebar + `<main>` present; page markup in the HTML |

- "HTML contains sidebar and page markup with JS disabled": met. Read this with the caveat below. Screenshot with JS disabled at 400 ms: `/tmp/ssr-probe/nojs-400ms.png` (sidebar painted).
- Caveat, a deliberate choice: the Suspense boundary streams the page into the same response, in a hidden segment that a ~1 KB inline script reveals. With JS fully off, the page markup is in the HTML but stays hidden; the sidebar is visible. Without the boundary, first paint would equal the page's server-data time (git + workspace registry: 2–37 s under today's load), not the shell. The main area is blank until the page streams; loading UI is item 2's.
- Hydration: 20 dashboard routes crawled in prod with JS. No React or hydration errors on any route, including browser `?file=` and `?mobileView=`, a stored sort preference, phone viewport, work-unit editors, workflows, pij, and settings.

## Auth-gate proofs (nav-wave-1 "terminal keeps working"), on the e37b1ea0d build

Server and sidecar ran on :3191/:4691, because :3101 is held on IPv4 by OrbStack container `osk-main-ops-1`. Both ran with `TMUX` unset and `TMUX_TMPDIR=/tmp/ssr-dashboard-tmux`. Scratch tmux sessions exist only on that private server.

| Check | localhost:3191 | 192.168.1.32:3191 |
|---|---|---|
| xterm mounts, WS to sidecar | yes (`ws://localhost:4691/terminal?session=...`) | yes (`ws://192.168.1.32:4691/...`) |
| Typing reaches the shell, output streams back (`echo SSR_PROOF_$((6*7))` → `SSR_PROOF_42` over WS) | yes | yes |
| Resize: `tput cols` follows the viewport, 1600 → 1000 px | 179 → 94 (page), 179 → 93 (overlay) | 179 → 94, 179 → 93 |
| Window strip (overlay header): `tmux new-window -d -n proofwinN` appears; clicking it sets `aria-pressed=true` | yes (1 → 2 windows) | yes (3 → 4 windows) |
| Console / page errors | none | none |

- LAN note: under prod, `/api/bootstrap/verify` sets `Secure`, and Chromium drops it over plain HTTP. For the LAN run I re-added the same cookie value without `Secure`. That bug is pre-existing and owned on the HTTPS list ("Secure follows the real protocol").
- `cg` CLI X-Local-Token: `node apps/cli/dist/cli.cjs remote-view list --workspace-path <worktree>` → `[]`, exit 0 (server discovered via `.chainglass/server.json`, port 3191).
- Remote view through `requireRemoteViewAccess`/`requireLocalAuth`: `GET /api/remote-view/sessions` from localhost gives 200 `{"sessions":[]}` with the token and 401 without.
- Real next-auth path (build with `DISABLE_AUTH=false DISABLE_GITHUB_OAUTH=false`):
  - `/api/auth/session` gives `null` without a session and the user with a minted Auth.js JWT.
  - The workspace page renders 200 with the minted session.
  - Unauthenticated workspace → 307 `/login`.
  - This found the `/login` loop (separate item below).

## Findings outside item 1

- `/login` redirect loop with OAuth on: prime assigned it to me. A failing test is written and passes with the fix. It lands after strip-067's `proxy.ts` is on main.
- `localhost-guard` trusts headers: prime assigned it to me, with conditions. It lands after `/login` and after crane's `instrumentation.ts`. Confirmed live on a read-only route: LAN + token + `Host: localhost` + `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` → 200 on `/api/remote-view/sessions`.
- `/api/terminal` answers 500 when no tmux server is running (seen on the private server before the first session existed).
- Pages prefetch `/workspaces/<slug>/agents?...`, which 404s (6 per workspace page load).
- `SecurityError: User activation is required.` on the terminal mobile view. [INFERENCE] from `features/067-question-popper/lib/desktop-notifications.ts:24` (`Notification.requestPermission()` without a gesture), which strip-067 removes.
